newsitem.title: USA: Medaphis says McDowell takes over as CEO.
newsitem.headline: Medaphis says McDowell takes over as CEO.

text.p: Medaphis Corp said on Thursday David McDowell took over as the company's chairman and chief executive officer.
McDowell replaces Randolph Brown, who has resigned to pursue personal interests, the company said.
McDowell joined Medaphis' board of directors on May 16.
He previously served as president, chief operating officer and director of McKesson Corp.
In a statement, Brown said, "I have enjoyed my nine years with the company and want only the best for the company and its customers, employees and shareholders."

Shares in Medaphis fell 60 percent in heavy trading in August after it said it expected a third quarter 1996 loss and said its 1997 earnings would fall well under previous expectations due to weakness in its Physician Services Corp unit and a reorganization of its Imonics unit.
Last week its stock fell more that 30 percent after it reported a third-quarter pro forma loss.
Also in August, a class action suit was filed against the company's alleging it and its senior executives misrepresented the company's conditions.
Medaphis provides transaction processing and information technology systems and services for clients in various markets, initially concentrated in health care.

Cowen and Co analyst Charles Trafton said Brown had been a key force in building Medaphis through a series of acquisitions. The company now appeared to be looking for a chief executive more focused on operations, he said.
"They've come up quite short of expectations on the operating front here so they've brought in an expert operator," Trafton said.
He noted McDowell's experience at International Business Machines Corp, where the new chief executive worked before going to McKesson.
In 29 years at IBM, McDowell held positions including general manager of IBM's National Service Division, responsible for IBM's customer support services.
